subject: ACME - SOC 2 and security follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>, ACME Security Team <security@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - SOC 2 and security follow-up / next steps

Hi John / ACME security team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we're all aligned. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain points & goals
- Need SOC 2 Type II evidence and recent controls mapping for vendor review
- Clarify audit log retention and access patterns (required for compliance review)
- Proof of recent penetration test and remediation timeline
- Data processing terms (DPA) and liability language for procurement

What we discussed / what Redwood provides
- SOC 2: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering 2025-09 through 2026-03) and control mapping to common customer controls.
- Audit logs: Default logs retained 90 days; we offer extended retention and export for customers with enterprise plans. Logs include access, admin actions, model inference metadata (no raw customer prompt content by default unless configured).
- Pen test evidence: We can provide a redacted executive summary and remediation attestations; full reports require an NDA/controlled sharing.
- DPA: Preliminary DPA draft attached (DPA_draft_ACME_v1.docx). We're open to the standard edits you listed; legal will review agreed changes.

Agreed next steps
1) I will send the SOC 2 extract, pen-test summary (redacted), and a control mapping spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow. (Attachments: redwood_soc2_report_v1.pdf, pen_test_summary.zip)
2) John / security to confirm whether 90-day retention meets requirements or if ACME needs >90/365/archival exports.
3) Procurement to review the DPA and propose any redlines; I'll loop in Legal if needed.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk through audit log schemas and access controls (proposed times below).

Proposed times for technical deep-dive (Pacific):
- Tue Mar 2: 10:00–11:00 / 15:00–16:00 ET
- Wed Mar 3: 09:00–10:00 / 14:00–15:00 ET

Attachments referenced: redwood_soc2_report_v1.pdf, pen_test_summary.zip, DPA_draft_ACME_v1.docx

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical
From: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: ACME - SOC 2 and security follow-up / next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) Audit logs: Can you confirm what fields are included in the inference metadata you mentioned (timestamps, user_id, request_id, model_version, input_size, response_size, any PII redaction flags)? We need to map to our control matrix.

2) Retention: 90 days is a starting point. Our security policy requires at least 365 days of event-level logs for certain systems; is extended retention available as an opt-in, and what are the costs/throughput impacts?

3) Pen test: We’ll need an executive summary and a statement of remediation for any high/critical findings. If full reports are behind an NDA, can you provide the process and timeline to get that in place?

4) DPA: Procurement will review the draft and push back on a couple of clauses. Who should we expect to coordinate with on redlines (legal@redwood.ai or you directly)?

If you can answer 1–3 in the thread we can triage before the technical deep-dive.

—John
John Doe
Head of Security, ACME Corp
j.doe@acme.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>, ACME Security Team <security@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - SOC 2 and security follow-up / next steps

John — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and attached evidence.

1) Inference metadata / audit log fields (high-level):
- timestamp
- request_id (UUID)
- customer_tenant_id / org_id
- api_key_id (masked)
- model_version
- endpoint/route
- caller_ip (masked when required)
- response_status / error codes
- token_count (input/output)
- admin_action flags (config changes, key rotations)

We will provide a schema extract in the Drive link.

2) Retention options:
- Default: 90 days (no extra cost)
- Extended: 365 days (configurable, added storage surcharge; can be exported to your S3/Cloud Storage for long-term archival)
- Export-only: continuous export to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) with retention per your policy (recommended for long-term compliance)

I’ve asked our infra team to provide a rough cost estimate for 365-day retention for ACME’s expected throughput; I’ll share when available.

3) Pen test evidence / NDA: Attached is the redacted executive summary (pen_test_summary.zip) and our standard controlled-sharing flow. For full reports we require an executed NDA and one-off access controls; typical turnaround is 3–5 business days after NDA.

4) DPA coordination: Please send redlines to legal@redwood.ai; I’ll be copied and will coordinate operational questions. We can also use the DocuSign link I’ll share once redlines are agreed.

Technical deep-dive: Tue Mar 2 at 10:00 PT works for our engineers. Monica will host and walk through the log schema and export options.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_report_v1.pdf, pen_test_summary.zip, DPA_draft_ACME_v1.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
